chain.label: Relief first officer requested an unusually early transfer of flight control
chain.trigger: I'm not going to sleep at all. I might come and sit for two hours

chain.label: Relief first officer, alone in the cockpit, manually disconnected the autopilot with no operational reason
chain.trigger: no autopilot disconnect warning tone was heard on the CVR recording... consistent with the autopilot being manually disconnected

caused_by.evidence: transfer of control this early in the flight was contrary to the EgyptAir practice typically agreed-upon by flight crews; the captain then left the cockpit, leaving the relief first officer alone at the controls

chain.label: Relief first officer manually retarded both throttle levers from cruise power to idle
chain.trigger: the throttle levers were moved from their cruise power setting to idle

caused_by.evidence: there was no logical operational reason for the relief first officer to disconnect the autopilot while in cruise flight over the ocean

chain.label: Relief first officer pushed the control column, producing an abrupt sustained nose-down elevator deflection and steep dive
chain.trigger: the FDR recorded an abrupt nose-down elevator movement... the airplane began to rapidly pitch nose down and descend

caused_by.evidence: the nose-down elevator movement began after the throttle levers started to move to idle
autopilot disconnect preceded the manual flight control inputs that followed

chain.label: Captain's nose-up recovery inputs and relief first officer's continued nose-down inputs produced an opposing, split elevator condition
chain.trigger: the captain repeatedly stated, 'Pull with me'... the elevator surfaces remained in a split condition with the left surface commanding nose up and the right surface commanding nose down

caused_by.evidence: the captain returned to the cockpit exclaiming, 'What's happening? What's happening?' as the dive continued

chain.label: Relief first officer moved both engine start levers to cutoff, shutting down the engines during the recovery attempt
chain.trigger: the engine start lever switches for both engines moved from the run to the cutoff position

caused_by.evidence: the evidence indicates that the relief first officer moved the engine start lever switches to the cutoff position, a counterproductive action in terms of recovery

chain.label: Airplane failed to recover and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean
chain.trigger: the airplane started a second descent, which continued until the airplane impacted the ocean

caused_by.evidence: a successful recovery, although possible, was not accomplished
efforts to recover the airplane after it lost electrical power were also complicated by the loss of electronic cockpit displays

chain.label: All 217 people on board were killed
chain.trigger: All 217 people on board were killed, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: crashed into the Atlantic Ocean about 60 miles south of Nantucket... All 217 people on board were killed
